name: ASAP1
description: First ASAP sensor, establishing the VSD/cpGFP architecture for fast, negative-going fluorescence responses to voltage.

kinetics.note: Amplitude-weighted means of the bi-exponential fit (St-Pierre 2014 Fig. 1e, HEK293A, 22°C). Activation (on): τ1 = 2.1 ms (60.2%), τ2 = 71.5 ms (39.8%) → τon = 0.602×2.1 + 0.398×71.5 = 29.7 ms. Deactivation/inactivation (off): τ1 = 2.0 ms (43.7%), τ2 = 50.8 ms (56.3%) → τoff = 0.437×2.0 + 0.563×50.8 = 29.5 ms. Previously stored only the fast components (2.1 / 2.0 ms), which severely understate the true response — Fig. 1e DOES report the slow τ2 numerically (71.5 / 50.8 ms), so the weighted mean is computable directly and a prior note claiming it was reported only as a ratio was incorrect.

Amplitude-weighted means of the bi-exponential fit (Chamberland/eLife 2017 Table 1, HEK293A, 22°C). The paper fit each response to a weighted sum of two time constants and explicitly 'focus here on the faster time constants'. Depolarization −70→+30 mV (on): τfast 2.9 ms (74%), τslow 161 ms (26%) → τon = 0.74×2.9 + 0.26×161 = 44.0 ms. Repolarization +30→−70 mV (off): τfast 2.3 ms (63%), τslow 177 ms (37%) → τoff = 0.63×2.3 + 0.37×177 = 66.9 ms. Previously stored the fast components (2.9 / 2.4 ms) — 2.4 did not even match the table's 2.3 ms repolarization τfast. Consistent with St-Pierre 2014 (29.7/29.5 weighted); Zou 2014 (6.7/11.6) reads a much smaller slow-component amplitude/τ.

Amplitude-weighted means of the bi-exponential fit (Zou 2014 Table 1): depolarizing (on) τfast 2.3 ms (88%), τslow 39 ms → τon = 0.88×2.3 + 0.12×39 = 6.7 ms; hyperpolarizing (off) τfast 3.0 ms (67%), τslow 29 ms → τoff = 0.67×3.0 + 0.33×29 = 11.6 ms. Previously stored the fast components (2.3 / 3.0 ms). Verified 2026-09-08 against the Table 1 row (ΔF/F per 100 mV 28.8; depolarizing step −70 → +30 mV, hyperpolarizing step +30 → −70 mV, 23°C, 6–9 cells, 3 W/cm²).

Amplitude-weighted means of the bi-exponential fit re-measured for ASAP1 in the ASAP3 paper (Villette 2019 Table S1, HEK293A, 23°C, n = 4 cells). Depolarization −70 → +30 mV (on): τfast 2.4 ± 0.2 ms (70 ± 3%), τslow 72 ± 2 ms → τon = 0.70×2.4 + 0.30×72 = 23.3 ms. Return from depolarization +30 → −70 mV (off): τfast 2.1 ± 0.4 ms (53 ± 5%), τslow 75 ± 2 ms → τoff = 0.53×2.1 + 0.47×75 = 36.4 ms. Added 2026-09-08; this is an independent re-measurement by the originating (Lin) lab, distinct from the St-Pierre 2014 Fig. 1e numbers. NOTE for future checkers: the Gong 2015 Science Table S2 ASAP1 row (τfast 2.1/τslow 72/60% fast; 2.0/51/44%) is the SAME data as St-Pierre 2014 Fig. 1e rounded (shared authors), NOT an independent measurement, and is deliberately NOT stored as a separate entry.

subthresholdData.note: Subthreshold voltage sensitivity ≈ 0.21 %/mV, derived from the Fig. 3b (top) quantification in voltage-clamped cultured rat hippocampal neurons: ASAP1 peak −ΔF/F was 1.20 / 2.05 / 2.85 / 4.52% for simulated subthreshold depolarization waveforms of 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 mV peak amplitude (17 ms peak FWHM, n = 6 neurons, 1P widefield, 22°C). Through-origin least squares over the four points gives 0.213 %/mV (free-intercept fit gives 0.215 %/mV with a ~0 intercept, i.e. the response is linear over this range). Read off the bar graph, so ±~5%. Comparable steady-state chord slope from the HEK293A F−V curve (Fig. 1d, −80 → −60 mV) is 0.31 %/mV; the neuronal waveform value is lower because these are brief transient responses, not steady-state steps. Cross-GEVI: ArcLight Q239 in the same panel gives ≈ 0.13 %/mV (0.80 / 1.63 / 2.12 / 2.28%).

photostabilityData.note: Origin-paper photobleaching in dissociated rat hippocampal neurons under continuous 470–490 nm widefield illumination at 0.12 mW/mm² (Fig. S9; four neurons imaged every 10 s for 4.5–15 min, F normalized to 1.0 at t=0). Mono-exponential photobleaching time constants were 41.7 / 35.7 / 32.3 / 30.3 min (mean 35.0 ± 2.5 min, also stated in the main text), so the fluorescence remaining after 15 min is exp(−15/35.0) = 65%. CORRECTED from a previously stored 74%, which corresponds to the SNR-decay time T(4→2) = 49.1 ± 9.8 min — a signal-to-noise metric, not the fluorescence photobleaching τ. The one neuron actually imaged for the full 15 min (gray trace, τ = 30.3 min) ended at F/F₀ ≈ 0.615, bracketing the 65% model value.

Gong 2015 Table S2 reports an ASAP1 bleaching rate of 0.3 ± 0.1% per s (n = 10 cells) under 480/470 nm one-photon epifluorescence at 15 mW/mm² at the specimen plane (stated in the Table S2 footnote), i.e. ≈ 91% remaining after 30 s.

Cross-GEVI from the FlicR1 origin paper. ASAP1 single-exponential photobleaching τ = 47 ± 1 s (n = 5 HEK293 cells) under continuous 488 nm at 10 W/cm² = 100 mW/mm² (Fig. 3I curves, Fig. 3J time constants), i.e. exp(−60/47) = 28% remaining at 1 min. Already at the 100 mW/mm², 1 min reference condition.

Fluorescence remaining after 1 min of continuous widefield 470–490 nm illumination at 11 mW/mm² in HEK293-Kir2.1 cells (ASAP1 blue trace of Fig. 1—figure supplement 3A; biexponential τ1 = 100 s / τ2 = 850 s per panel B → F/F₀ = 0.72 at t = 60 s). Consistent with the digitized photobleach curve stored for the same figure. sourceFigure was previously the ambiguous "Fig. S3" — this eLife paper has BOTH a Figure 1—figure supplement 3 (1P photostability in immortalized cells) and a Figure 2—figure supplement 3 (photobleaching in neurons); this value is the former, matching the ASAP2s page.

apWidthData.sample: Rat cultured hippocampal neurons, current-triggered single AP, in vitro
apWidthData.note: Optical single-AP FWHM stated in the ASAP1 origin paper (St-Pierre 2014): 'The corresponding FWHM of the fluorescence responses (bottom) were 3.7 ms and 6.5 ms for ASAP1 and ArcLight Q239, respectively' (Fig. 1f). Measured under 1P widefield in cultured rat hippocampal neurons responding to current-triggered single APs, imaged at 827 Hz with 4×4 binning (Methods), at 22°C. The electrical AP FWHM in the same neuron was 3.3 ms (voltage trace), so the optical width is only modestly broadened by the sensor's fast kinetics. Cross-GEVI: ArcLight Q239 optical FWHM 6.5 ms in the same panel.

apWidthData.sample: Organotypic hippocampal slice cultures, current-triggered single AP, two-photon RAMP (FEVIR)
apWidthData.note: Optical single-AP duration (full-width at half-maximum) stated in the ASAP2s origin paper (primary subject ASAP2s): 'ASAP1 exhibited AP-induced transients with a mean time-to-peak of 3.1 ms and a duration (full-width at half-maximum) of 3.8 ms' (Fig. 6D,E), measured under two-photon FEVIR (RAMP microscopy) in organotypic hippocampal slice cultures, oversampled at 3700 Hz, at room temperature (22°C). ASAP2s in the same experiment was 21.1 ms.

apWidthData.sample: Rat, cultured hippocampal neurons, in vitro
apWidthData.note: Optical spike width (FWHM of the optical AP) read from the Fig. 2J bar graph in cultured hippocampal neurons responding to current-triggered APs, 1P widefield. ASAP1 ≈ 9.0 ms, ASAP2s ≈ 17.4 ms; the electrical AP widths in the same neurons were 4.2 ms (ASAP1) / 4.6 ms (ASAP2s) per the caption, so the optical widths are broadened by the sensors' response kinetics (ASAP2s' slower repolarization gives the wider optical spike). Imaging rate is the Methods-stated 1 kHz widefield optical-AP rate; the width is kinetics-dominated (>> the 1 ms frame period), not frame-rate-limited. Recording temperature not stated for this panel. Distinct from the 2P/organotypic-slice value (Fig. 6E) and the HEK293 value.

apWidthData.sample: Mouse, cultured primary cortical/hippocampal neurons (P0.5), in vitro
apWidthData.note: Cross-GEVI value from the Milosevic 2020 eNeuro GEVI-comparison study (in-vitro testing of Archon1, ArcLightD, ASAP1, ASAP2s, ASAP3b, Bongwoori-Pos6, FlicR1, chi-VSFP-Butterfly; no single primary subject). Half-width (FWHM) of the optically recorded action potential: 'The half-width of optically recorded action potentials was on average 6.1 ± 0.3 ms (n = 9), 8.5 ± 0.2 ms (n = 3), 12.3 ± 0.7 (n = 6), and 33.1 ± 2.6 (n = 6), respectively, for Archon1, ASAP1, ASAP2 and Bongwoori' — so ASAP1 = 8.5 ± 0.2 ms (n = 3). The ASAP1-specific data live in Fig. 1A (A1 shows a cell 'transduced with pCAG-ASAP1'; A3 shows the optical AP half-width); the half-width sentence cites Fig. 1A1–D collectively across all four GEVIs (Fig. 1D is the Archon1 panel, not ASAP1). Primary mouse cortical/hippocampal neuron cultures (P0.5, Swiss Webster; Methods p.266), current-triggered single APs, 1P widefield NeuroCCD imaging at 500 frames/s (Fig. 1A caption); ASAP1 excitation 480/40 nm, emission 535/50 nm, 5.05 mW/mm²; recording temperature not stated. The optical half-width was on average 741 ± 25% of the simultaneously patch-recorded electrical AP half-width (i.e. ~7× wider), reflecting the sensor's response kinetics. Distinct from the origin-paper HEK/neuron value (Fig. 1f) and the eLife 2P/1P values.

photobleach.note: ORIGIN-PAPER 1P photobleach (St-Pierre 2014 Fig. S9), digitized 2026-09-08. Dissociated rat hippocampal neurons, continuous 470–490 nm widefield at 0.12 mW/mm², imaged every 10 s, F normalized to 1.0 at t=0; four neurons are plotted (red/blue/green/gray) with mono-exponential τ = 41.7 / 35.7 / 32.3 / 30.3 min (mean 35.0 ± 2.5 min). The stored curve is the GRAY neuron — the only trace covering the full 0–15 min window (the other three stop at 4.5–5 min) — extracted by colour-masking the markers and calibrating against the axis ticks, then overlay-verified against the figure. A least-squares mono-exponential through the digitized points gives τ = 1766 s (29.4 min), within 3% of the paper's own published 30.3 min for this trace, and a biexponential does not improve the residual (rms 0.0087 vs 0.0097) — so mono-exponential is the correct model, as the paper states. t₇₅ = 1766·ln(4/3) = 508 s (8.5 min), well inside the digitized window; direct interpolation of the digitized points gives 492 s, and the 4-neuron MEAN τ of 35.0 min would give t₇₅ = 604 s. `intensityMWmm2` is deliberately OMITTED: linear dose-scaling from 0.12 to the 100 mW/mm² reference is an 833× extrapolation and disagrees ~26× with the direct 100 mW/mm² measurement in Abdelfattah 2016 Fig. 3I (t₇₅ 16 s) stored on this page, so a dose-scaled number here would be misleading. ASAP1 is the only sensor in this figure, so there are no cross-overlay companions.

Cross-GEVI from the ASAP2s paper (primary subject ASAP2s). ASAP1 (blue) biexponential τ1=100 s (55%) + τ2=850 s (45%) per Fig. 1-fig.suppl.3B. t75≈52 s, t50≈150 s. Origin-paper 1P photobleach, Fig. 1—figure supplement 3A: HEK293-Kir2.1 cells, continuous widefield 470–490 nm at 11 mW/mm², emission 525/50 nm, normalized to 1.0 at t=0. The stored curve is generated from the paper's OWN published fit (Fig. 1—figure supplement 3B) rather than pixel-digitized, because ASAP1/ASAP2s/ArcLight overlap almost exactly in panel A; the fit endpoints match the panel-A traces at 5 min. All co-plotted sensors (ASAP1, ASAP2s, ArcLight Q239; ASAP1::EGFP has no page) share this source+sourceFigure so they cross-overlay.

Cross-GEVI value from the FlicR1 origin paper (Abdelfattah 2016, J Neurosci 36:2458–2472; primary subject FlicR1). ASAP1 = green curve in Fig. 3I. Digitized (HSV color separation) from the 1P photobleaching panel Fig. 3I: normalized fluorescence vs time for FlicR1 (red), ArcLight Q239 (black), ASAP1 (green) in HEK293 cells under continuous 488 nm illumination at 10 W/cm² = 100 mW/mm², normalized to 1.0 at t=0. ASAP1 is the LEAST photostable of the three (fastest decay); model-free t75 ≈ 16 s (biexponential fit), consistent with the paper's single-exponential τ = 47 ± 1 s (→ t75 ≈ 14 s). Already at the 100 mW/mm² reference. Distinct from this page's other photobleach entry (ASAP2s paper Fig. 1—fig. suppl. 3A @ 11 mW/mm²). Cross-plotted with FlicR1 and ArcLight Q239 from the same Fig. 3I.

TWO-PHOTON photobleach (standalone — NOT intensity-normalized or comparable to the 1P entries; no intensityMWmm2). Cross-GEVI value from the FlicR1 origin paper (Abdelfattah 2016, J Neurosci 36:2458–2472; primary subject FlicR1). Digitized from Fig. 4C: point-scan fluorescence vs time for ASAP1 excited at 950 nm (blue) and FlicR1 at 1120 nm (red), ~1 mW at both wavelengths, tuned to ~400 counts per bin initially, sampled at 100 Hz, HEK293 cells; normalized to the first-frame value (F₀ ≈ 454 counts). ASAP1 bleaches very rapidly under 2P, so a model-free t75 lands deep in the fast transient — the sustained-phase t50 ≈ 0.84 s is stored instead. FlicR1 is ~an order of magnitude more 2P-photostable (t50 8.6 s vs 0.84 s), as the paper states. Cross-plotted with FlicR1 from the same Fig. 4C.

spectrum.name: ASAP1
spectrum.note: No one-photon excitation/emission spectrum is published for ASAP1/ASAP2s: the eLife 2017 paper reports only two-photon excitation spectra (Fig. 1E) and the St-Pierre 2014 ASAP1 paper reports none. ASAP1's fluorophore is cpsfGFP-OPT, a circularly permuted superfolder GFP, so the FPbase Superfolder GFP excitation/emission curve is used as a fluorophore proxy. ASAP2s (ASAP1 + R415Q) shares this fluorophore. Replaces a curve that was a verbatim copy of the FPbase EGFP spectrum.

voltage.name: ASAP1
voltage.note: Re-digitized (2026-09-08) marker-by-marker from St-Pierre 2014 Fig. 1d (mean ASAP1 response vs transmembrane voltage, HEK293A, n = 10 cells, 22°C, normalized to the −70 mV holding potential). The nine plotted command steps are −120, −100, −80, −60, −40, −20, 0, +30 and +50 mV; the −70 mV point is the paper's own normalization baseline and is therefore exactly 0 by definition (the digitized curve crosses zero at ≈ −71 mV, consistent). Paper-stated anchors reproduced exactly: +23.4% at −120 mV and +11.7% at −100 mV (50 and 30 mV hyperpolarizations, main text) and −17.5% at +30 mV (the 100-mV depolarization from −70 mV, main text); the digitized +50 mV value (−21.1%) is consistent with the stated −36.3% total change from −120 to +50 mV (23.4% → −21.4% predicted). REPLACES a previous array [−120,−100,−70,−50,−30,0,30] → [23.4,11.7,0,−6,−11,−15.5,−17.5] whose −50/−30 mV points were not measured step voltages at all and whose 0 mV value (−15.5%) disagreed with the figure (−12.8%).
